sec: ATN phases and the hypercalcemia/hypernatremia note · p800

items.q: Match the three phases of ATN described — 1) Phase 1 tubular injury  2) Phase 2 tubuloglomerular feedback  3) Phase 3 … A) ↓GFR from adenosine-mediated afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction  B) Loss of solutes and water  C) Recovery
items.exp: ATN phases: 1 — tubular injury with loss of solutes and water; 2 — tubuloglomerular feedback → ↓GFR; 3 — recovery. (Book p800)

items.q: In ATN, the fall in urine output is mediated by:
items.exp: ATN phase 2: ↓urine output from adenosine-mediated afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction, with ↑S. phosphorus, ↓S. Ca²⁺, ↑mg²⁺ and hyponatremia all reducing GFR. (Book p800)

items.q: Match each ATN electrolyte acid-base change — 1) Serum phosphorus  2) Serum calcium  3) Serum magnesium  4) Serum sodium … A) ↓  B) ↑  C) ↑  D) ↓ (hyponatremia)
items.exp: ATN phase 2: ↑S. phosphorus, ↓S. Ca²⁺, ↑mg²⁺ and hyponatremia, all grouped with the fall in GFR. (Book p800)

items.q: Match the complications of ATN — 1) Uremia  2) Volume overload  3) Acidosis  4) Potassium … A) ↑K⁺  B) NAGMA  C) Present  D) Present
items.exp: ATN complications: uremia, volume overload, acidosis (NAGMA — normal anion gap metabolic acidosis) and ↑K⁺. (Book p800)

items.q: Fill up: The acidosis of ATN is described as ______.
items.exp: ATN complications include acidosis (NAGMA) and ↑K⁺ along with uremia and volume overload. (Book p800)

items.q: Hypercalcemia and hypernatremia are not seen in AKI.
opts: False — both are typical of AKI
False — hypercalcemia is typical but hypernatremia is not
True, but only for stage 3 AKI
items.exp: Note: hypercalcemia and hypernatremia are not seen in AKI (indeed calcium falls and hyponatremia occurs), whereas hyperkalaemia and acidosis are characteristic. (Book p800)

items.q: A patient with ATN is in the recovery phase. Which phase number and description apply?
opts: Phase 1 — tubular injury with loss of solutes and water
There is no recovery phase in ATN
items.exp: ATN phases are 1 — tubular injury, 2 — tubuloglomerular feedback with ↓GFR, 3 — recovery. (Book p800)

items.q: All but one of the following biochemical changes are seen in ATN. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: In ATN, S. Ca²⁺ falls (↓); phosphorus, magnesium and uric acid rise with hyponatremia. (Book p800)
